subject: Clarify discount approval and commit status for Halcyon SOW
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify discount approval and commit status for Halcyon SOW

Team — quick one. Halcyon (HL-2026-0421) pushed the SOW and procurement asked for a signed doc by end of week. Procurement flagged a 25% one-time onboarding credit in the attached SOW and wants to know if we can approve that concession without dealdesk escalation. Finance is asking whether this should be recorded as a committed ARR adjustment or a one-time credit that doesn't affect the forecast commit.

Context:
- ACV on the SOW is $450k year 1, onboarding credit ~ $112.5k one-time.
- Sales position: need the concession to close this quarter.
- Pricing: Vanessa, you own the gate here — can this be approved under our micro-concession band?
- Deal desk / Finance: Karthik / Laura, how does this flow into the commit? If we treat $112.5k as discount against first-year ARR, it materially reduces the Q3 committed number.

Asks:
- Vanessa: quick approval decision or specific counter-proposal (e.g., reduce onboarding credit to 15%).
- Karthik / Laura: classification recommended for forecasting (Committed ARR adjustment | One-time credit | Hold as pending non-commit).
- Priyom: hold cadence with Halcyon — can we get a 48-hour extension if we need dealdesk review?

Attaching latest SOW and my pricing breakdown. If we escalate, I want to include a short justification (deal strategic, reference customer expansion potential).

Thanks —
Michael Grant
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

On Tue, Jul 22, 2026 at 09:12 AM Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — quick one. Halcyon (HL-2026-0421) pushed the SOW and procurement asked for a signed doc by end of week...

Quick read: agreeing we need to be careful with commit treatment. My initial take: a one-time onboarding credit normally should not alter committed ARR unless we explicitly reduce the annual price in the contract language. Does the SOW reduce recurring subscription fees or is the credit applied as a separate invoice line? I can push a fast-track to dealdesk but need these details to justify a concession exception.

Questions for Michael: can you confirm whether the onboarding credit is written as a deduction from Year 1 subscription fees (line item) or as a separate 'professional services discount' one-time? If it's the former, expect finance to want ARR adjustments.

If it's ambiguous, propose we:
- Option A: Convert to 15% onboarding credit and label it professional services credit (non-recurring). No ARR change.
- Option B: Keep 25% as-is but route through Deal Desk; expect review time ~48 hours.

I can start the Deal Desk ticket now if you prefer.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick turnaround, Michael and Karthik. Our procurement team needs the signed SOW to start onboarding the integration team — they pushed the timeline up. The credit is intended to offset initial setup fees (one-time) but Halcyon prefers to see it on the face of the SOW as a 25% onboarding credit applied to the first invoice.

If you can’t approve 25% immediately, we are open to 15% but would prefer to keep the remainder as a waived implementation fee within the first 30 days. Time sensitivity: can you confirm by EOD Thursday PT so we can align vendor approvals and internal scheduling?

Michael / team — read and propose the following:
- Approve 15% onboarding credit as an authorized micro-concession (no dealdesk).
- Remaining 10% can be converted to a one-time waived implementation fee (professional services credit) that we record as non-recurring; does not change committed ARR.
- Require Halcyon to accept amended language: "25% onboarding consideration comprised of a 15% subscription credit and a 10% implementation fee credit. Implementation credit is non-recurring and applies to invoice #1 only."

If sales wants full 25% against subscription line items, route to Deal Desk for exception approval (I will support but expect 24–48 hour turnaround). Given the time pressure, I'd approve the 15% + 10% split above to keep the close this week while preserving forecast integrity.

Vanessa Ortiz
Manager, Pricing & Packaging
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

Subject: RE: Clarify discount approval and commit status for Halcyon SOW

Natalie — thanks, and appreciate the flexibility. Halcyon: we can do the 25% total consideration split as follows to preserve forecasting clarity: 15% applied as a subscription credit (affects invoice but recorded as a promotional credit for Year 1; note: this will not be treated as an ARR reduction under our accounting guidance) and 10% recorded as a non-recurring professional services credit (implementation fee waiver). Vanessa and Finance have approved this treatment; Laura will note the commit classification in the forecast.

Next steps:
- Natalie: please confirm acceptance of the amended language by replying to this thread.
- Karthik / Priyom: update HubSpot deal HL-2026-0421 with the concession notes and mark stage as Commit - Subject to SOW signature (do not lower forecast until invoice attachment posted).
- Laura: please confirm the forecast classification and whether any manual adjustments are needed in the Q3 commit ledger.

Thanks all — aiming to get countersigned SOW by EOD Friday.

Michael Grant
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
